## Hinge question · Infinitely many values {#l1-hinge}

```{=html}
<div data-module="hinge" data-correct="3" class="hinge reciprocal-hinge">
<p class="hinge-question">A coin is tossed until the first head appears. For a completed trial, let <span data-math="N">N</span> be the number of tosses, and define <span data-math="X=\dfrac{1}{N}">X = 1/N</span>. Which statement is correct?</p>
<div class="hinge-toolbar"><div class="time" role="timer" aria-label="Time remaining">1:30</div><div class="toolbar"><label>Seconds <select class="timer-duration" aria-label="Question duration"><option selected>30</option><option>45</option><option>60</option><option>90</option><option>120</option></select></label><button class="timer-start primary">Start</button><button class="reset-question">Reset</button></div></div>
<div class="choices">
<button class="choice" data-answer="1" aria-pressed="false"><b>1</b><span><span data-math="X">X</span> is continuous because infinitely many values are possible.</span></button>
<button class="choice" data-answer="2" aria-pressed="false"><b>2</b><span><span data-math="X">X</span> is continuous because it can take any real value between <span data-math="0">0</span> and <span data-math="1">1</span>.</span></button>
<button class="choice" data-answer="3" aria-pressed="false"><b>3</b><span><span data-math="X">X</span> is discrete, with possible values <span data-math="1,\dfrac12,\dfrac13,\dfrac14,\ldots">1, 1/2, 1/3, 1/4, …</span>.</span></button>
<button class="choice" data-answer="4" aria-pressed="false"><b>4</b><span><span data-math="X">X</span> is discrete, with possible values <span data-math="0,1,\dfrac12,\dfrac13,\dfrac14,\ldots">0, 1, 1/2, 1/3, 1/4, …</span>.</span></button>
</div>
<div class="hinge-bottom"><p>Fist on chest. Think quietly. On “show”, hold up 1–4 fingers.</p><button class="reveal-answer primary">Reveal answer</button></div>
<div class="hinge-explanation" hidden>3. The values can be listed using the positive integers. They do not fill an interval, and no completed trial gives <span data-math="X=0">X = 0</span>.</div>
</div>
```

::: notes
Additional challenge for the Extension 1 class. This replaces the repeated running-time hinge; keep the “Try the distinction” activities unchanged. Allow 90 seconds by default, using the adjustable timer. Everyone starts with a fist on their chest and thinks independently. On your “show” cue, everyone holds up 1–4 fingers simultaneously. Collect responses before revealing; timer expiry must not reveal the answer.

Correct answer: 3. For completed trials, $N$ is a positive integer. Hence $X$ takes the values $1,\frac12,\frac13,\frac14,\ldots$. There are infinitely many possible values, including non-integers, but they can be listed using the positive integers and do not fill an interval. Every value is positive: approaching zero does not make zero an attainable value. “Completed trial” makes clear that the question concerns a finite number of tosses ending in a head; no discussion of non-terminating trials or formal probability distributions is required.

- 1: confuses infinitely many possible values with continuous variation.
- 2: assumes that every real value between the extremes is possible.
- 4: confuses getting arbitrarily close to zero with actually reaching zero.

Ready: ask “Could $X=0.4$? Explain.” It would require $N=2.5$ tosses, so it is impossible. Then proceed to Example 3.2.

Divided: have pairs list the first six values, then reconsider whether they include every real number between 0 and 1, or include 0. Re-poll on “show”.

Further explanation needed: connect each positive integer $N$ to its single reciprocal. Ask whether 0 or 0.4 appears in this list, then re-poll. Emphasise that discrete values need not be integers or form a finite set.
:::
